transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Professor Snape, sir? I was just wondering... what if, instead of stirring clockwise, I stirred the potion in a figure-eight pattern? Would that make it more... artistic?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: "Artistic?" I glower at the蠢 boy. "Potions are not a form of art, Mr. Connolly. They are a precise and exacting science. Stirring in a figure-eight pattern will do nothing but ensure you fail your next assignment. Focus on the correct technique, not on... whatever notions of creativity you've conjured up."

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: But what if I put the ingredients in backwards? Like, the last ingredient first? Does the cauldron even know the difference?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: The cauldron does not 'know' anything, you imbecile! It reacts to the sequence in which ingredients are added. Adding them in reverse order will result in a useless, possibly dangerous concoction. Pay attention, and stop trying to reinvent centuries of established potion-making practices. Now, if you have no further... original contributions to offer, perhaps we could focus on the correct way to prepare a basic Draught of Peace?

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: What if I used a Muggle pot instead of a cauldron? Would it still work? My mum makes soup in one and it tastes fine.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Mr. Connolly, this is preposterous! A Muggle pot is not enchanted, lacks the magical properties of a cauldron, and is entirely unsuitable for brewing potions. This is not a culinary experiment. Potions require specific magical reactions that can only occur in a cauldron. If you continue to equate potion-making with cooking, you will never succeed in this subject. Do I need to remind you that a single teaspoon of incorrectly brewed potion can have dire consequences? Now, attend to your workbook, and let's attempt the next exercise before we waste any more time on your... peculiar theories.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: But sir, what if I just... shook the cauldron instead of stirring? Wouldn't that mix everything faster?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: You would shake a cauldron? How... original. I'm certain your innovative 'shaking' method will revolutionize the art of... no, I mean the science of potion-making. But perhaps you should consider that a gentle stir is far more effective in achieving the desired result. A violent shake could agitate the contents too much, causing them to react in unpredictable ways. Now, unless you're planning to take a broomstick to the cauldron in your next 'breakthrough' attempt, I suggest you focus on the correct stirring technique. Otherwise, you may find yourself repeating this remedial session for the rest of the term.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: What if I used my wand to stir it? Like a big magical spoon? Would that make it more powerful?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Using your wand as a stirrer? How... enterprising of you. While I'm sure this method would indeed make the potion 'powerful,' it would likely be far too powerful to be of any use. And, I might add, potentially dangerous. A wand's magic is not designed to be channeled into a cauldron in such a manner. It could easily cause the potion to react in a way that would either render it useless or create a substance so potent it could be considered... volatile. Focus, Mr. Connolly, on the simple, tried and tested methods of potion-making. There is no need for such... unorthodox approaches. Now, if we are done discussing your... innovative ideas, perhaps we could finally move on to the actual task at hand?

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: But what if I just... didn't stir it at all? What if I just let it sit there and hoped it would mix itself?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Mr. Connolly, your... suggestions are becoming increasingly... inefficient. If you propose to let a potion mix itself, you may as well suggest we cancel the next Great Exhibition of Arithmancy and replace it with a poetry recital. Potion-making is not about 'hoping' for a result; it requires precise actions and careful attention. A potion that is not stirred will not mix, and you will end up with a cauldron full of separate ingredients instead of a coherent concoction. I suggest you reconsider your approach to this subject. It may not be as... artistic or... easy as you seem to believe. Now, if we are to make any progress today, we need to focus on the correct methods of preparation. Let us begin by reviewing the correct stirring technique, unless you have any more... original ideas to share?

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: What if I stirred it with a feather? Like a quill? Would that make it more... scholarly?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Mr. Connolly, I am beginning to wonder if you are attempting to jest with me or if you genuinely do not grasp the gravity of potion-making. Stirring a potion with a feather would serve no purpose other than to waste my time and yours. It is not a scholarly pursuit, it is a... nonsensical notion. A quill is for writing, not for brewing. If you persist in this... whimsical approach, you may find yourself writing more essays than brewing potions. Now, unless you are prepared to demonstrate that you can follow a simple recipe without further... creative deviations, I suggest you pack up your... feather and go. We seem to be at an impasse in our... tutorial.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: But sir, what if I just... whispered the instructions to the potion? Would it listen?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Mr. Connolly, this is... preposterous. Whispering to a potion is akin to expecting a teapot to brew tea upon request. Potions are not sentient beings; they do not respond to... verbal urgings. They require precise ingredients, accurate measurements, and... meticulous preparation. Your... whimsical approach to potion-making is a recipe for disaster. If you continue in this vein, you may find yourself in the infirmary more often than in the classroom. I suggest, for the sake of your own well-being, that you abandon these... eccentric notions and focus on the tried and tested methods of potion preparation. If not, I am prepared to recommend additional... 'remedial' sessions to the head of your house. Now, unless you have any more... original ideas to share, let us proceed with the actual task at hand.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: What if I just... closed my eyes and pointed at the ingredients? Would that be a good way to choose them?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Mr. Connolly, I see we are at a crossroads in your... academic journey. If you believe that selecting ingredients by... pointing with your eyes closed is a sound method, I would be remiss if I did not inform you that you are grossly misunderstanding the nature of potion-making. This is not a game of chance, but a precise art that requires knowledge, skill, and attention to detail. If you continue to approach it with such... casual disregard, you may find yourself well-suited to a career in... magical guesswork. However, I suspect even that field would require a modicum of... intellectual engagement greater than what you are currently demonstrating. Now, if we are to salvage anything from this... tutoring session, I propose we focus on the correct identification and measurement of ingredients, unless you have any further... innovative suggestions to offer.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: What if I just... used my own tears as an ingredient? Would that make the potion more... emotional?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Mr. Connolly, I am... speechless. Using your own tears as an ingredient? I can only assume you are attempting to... poeticize a scientific process. Potions do not require emotional input, nor do they benefit from... personalized fluids. Such an approach would render the potion entirely ineffective and potentially... unsanitary. If you persist in this... emotionalized view of potion-making, I fear you will find little success in our... academic endeavors. I suggest you refocus your efforts on the... objective and rational aspects of the subject matter. If not, I am inclined to wonder if you are even capable of comprehending the... fundamental principles of potion-making. Now, unless you have any further... artistic interpretations to share, I propose we attempt to complete an actual potion today, if it is not too much to ask for your... undivided attention.
